name: NepalKit
description: Today's Bikram Sambat date in the macOS menu bar and on Apple Watch. Nepal Time, offline conversion, Siri & Shortcuts.
osps_ac_01_01_justification: Single-maintainer repository owned by a GitHub user account, not an organisation. GitHub provides no repository-level or organisation-level MFA enforcement for repositories owned by a user account, so there is no enforcement mechanism for this project to configure. GOVERNANCE.md names the sole principal.
osps_ac_02_01_justification: GitHub requires manual, per-account permission assignment: a collaborator can only be added, and their role chosen, by an explicit action of the repository owner. There are no teams, organisation roles, or automated grants. Policy in GOVERNANCE.md.
osps_ac_03_01_justification: Branch ruleset 'main' (id 24116591, enforcement active) contains a pull_request rule, so a direct push to the default branch is rejected, and a non_fast_forward rule blocks force-pushes. The repository owner is a bypass actor (bypass_mode: always); this is disclosed in GOVERNANCE.md and docs/security-assessment.md finding F3.
osps_ac_03_02_justification: The same branch ruleset contains a deletion rule, so the primary branch cannot be deleted. Visible under Settings > Rules > Rulesets.
osps_br_01_01_justification: Untrusted metadata is validated before use. release-tag.yml validates the tag against ^v[0-9]+[.][0-9]+[.][0-9]+$ and re-derives the version from project.pbxproj before it reaches any step; pull-request SHAs are passed through env: rather than interpolated into a shell; event_name and ref_type are compared as quoted strings inside job-level if: conditions, which GitHub evaluates before the job exists.
osps_br_01_03_justification: No pull_request-triggered workflow references any secret, and every pull-request build runs with CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO. Every workflow declares permissions explicitly and release-tag.yml declares permissions: {} at the top level, so no step inherits a default read/write token. Signing and notarization credentials are not in CI at all. See docs/secrets-policy.md.
osps_br_03_01_justification: Every official channel is encrypted in transit: git clone over HTTPS, releases over HTTPS, the Sparkle feed at https://dibas-np.github.io/NepalKit/appcast.xml over HTTPS, and the Homebrew tap over HTTPS. No plaintext http:// endpoint appears in any official channel; the only plain-HTTP strings in the repository are the Apple plist DTD and the Sparkle XML namespace URI, neither of which is fetched.
osps_br_03_02_justification: Release artifacts are signed with a Developer ID Application certificate (team CA89X9954L) with the hardened runtime, notarized by Apple and stapled; scripts/package-release.sh fails the release if the hardened runtime flag is absent. The update feed carries an Ed25519 signature and the app refuses a feed without one, so a tampered feed cannot redirect an installation. The Homebrew cask digest is computed only after the downloaded app passes spctl -a -t execute, xcrun stapler validate and a signing-identity check.
osps_br_07_01_justification: .gitignore excludes .env, build/, DerivedData/, .build/ and .swiftpm/. GitHub secret scanning and secret scanning push protection are both enabled on the repository, so a push introducing a detected credential is blocked before it reaches the branch.
osps_do_01_01_justification: README.md documents installation, the menu-bar item, the popover, Settings, date conversion in both directions, Siri and Shortcuts, and the Apple Watch app and its four complication styles.
osps_do_02_01_justification: SUPPORT.md documents where to report defects, what a good report contains, the expectation that an official Nepali Patro comparison is included, and that issues are the whole of the support channel.
osps_gv_02_01_justification: GitHub Issues are enabled on the repository, and SUPPORT.md names them as the channel for bugs, feature requests and usage obstacles, with a pointer away from issues for security problems.
osps_gv_03_01_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md documents the contribution process end to end: the calendar-provenance bar, local setup, the eleven gates run by scripts/check-all.sh, style, decision records, pull request expectations, the DCO, and how reviews are conducted.
osps_le_02_01_justification: GPL-3.0-or-later, an OSI-approved and FSF-free licence, in the LICENSE file at the repository root.
osps_le_02_02_justification: Released software assets are covered by GPL-3.0-or-later. The one vendored third-party component, the askbuddie calendar base table, is MIT-licensed and its complete licence text (MIT License, Copyright (c) 2023 Ask Buddie) ships inside the app bundle at NepalKit.app/Contents/Resources/NepalKitCore_NepalKitCore.bundle/Contents/Resources/AskBuddie-LICENSE.txt. See SOURCES.md.
osps_le_03_01_justification: The source-code licence is in the LICENSE file at the repository root.
osps_le_03_02_justification: LICENSE is a declared resource of the NepalKit target and is present in the shipped product at NepalKit.app/Contents/Resources/LICENSE (GNU General Public License Version 3, 29 June 2007), so the licence accompanies the released asset.
osps_qa_01_01_justification: Public repository at the static URL https://github.com/dibas-np/NepalKit
osps_qa_01_02_justification: The full commit history, author attribution and timestamps are publicly readable, and the branch ruleset's non_fast_forward rule prevents history from being rewritten on the default branch.
osps_qa_02_01_justification: Package.resolved is tracked at NepalKit.xcodeproj/project.xcworkspace/xcshareddata/swiftpm/Package.resolved and pins Sparkle 2.10.0. NepalKitCore and the app-test harness declare no external dependencies. The pin that governs resolution is the exactVersion requirement in project.pbxproj, which docs/dependencies.md records.
osps_qa_04_01_justification: The project is a single repository and compiles no additional codebases into a release.
osps_qa_05_01_justification: No generated executable artifact is tracked. .gitignore excludes build/, DerivedData/, .build/ and .swiftpm/, and no tracked path lies under those directories.
osps_qa_05_02_justification: The only non-text tracked files are nine SVG icon sources and six PNG documentation and evidence screenshots. No executable binaries, libraries, frameworks or archives are tracked.
osps_vm_02_01_justification: SECURITY.md publishes a security contact address and directs reporters to GitHub Security Advisories on this repository, with an explicit instruction not to open a public issue.
osps_ac_04_01_justification: Every workflow declares permissions explicitly rather than inheriting the repository default, and release-tag.yml declares permissions: {} at the top level. macos26-floor.yml records that omitting the block means every step gets the default token, which for a public repository is usually read/write on contents.
osps_br_02_01_justification: Each release is a distinct SemVer tag, from v1.0 through v1.6.0. release-tag.yml's preflight job refuses any tag whose name does not match the MARKETING_VERSION of the NepalKit target, so a version cannot repeat or drift from the app.
osps_br_04_01_justification: CHANGELOG.md records functional and security-relevant changes per released version, and the same notes are published per release and shipped in the update appcast. Security-relevant entries are called out, for example the end-to-end signed update channel in 1.4.1.
osps_br_05_01_justification: Dependencies are ingested with SwiftPM. The Sparkle package is pinned to exactVersion in project.pbxproj with a tracked Package.resolved, and the freshness of that pin is checked on a monthly schedule. The one build-time tool not covered by a package manager, SwiftLint, is fetched by scripts/swiftlint.sh with a pinned version and a hard-coded sha256 that must match, over HTTPS with a scheme downgrade refused.
osps_br_06_01_justification: The app is signed with a Developer ID Application certificate with the hardened runtime, notarized by Apple and stapled. The update feed is Ed25519-signed, and scripts/verify-appcast.py verifies each enclosure's declared length and signature against the public key committed to Info.plist before the feed is published or deployed. The Homebrew cask records a sha256 of the DMG, computed only after spctl, stapler and signing-identity checks pass on the downloaded bytes.
osps_do_06_01_justification: docs/dependencies.md documents the complete dependency inventory, why each dependency was selected, how each pin is obtained, and how each is tracked and refreshed, including the Dependabot coverage limit.
osps_do_07_01_justification: README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md document the required toolchain (Xcode 27 or later), the deployment floor (macOS 26.6 for the app, watchOS 26 for the Watch products), the Swift 6 language mode requirement, and every build, test and verification command.
osps_gv_01_01_justification: GOVERNANCE.md names the project's sole member with access to sensitive resources: Dibas Sigdel (@dibas-np), who holds all repository, release and signing authority.
osps_gv_01_02_justification: GOVERNANCE.md's 'Who decides' and 'What that means in practice' sections describe the maintainer's responsibilities for merge decisions, breaking changes and supported-range narrowing, releases, and the fact that licensing cannot be changed by contributors.
osps_gv_03_02_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md sets out the requirements for acceptable contributions: CODING_STANDARDS.md as a binding standard, the eleven local and CI gates and their order, the policy that a behaviour change ships with a test in the same commit, when a change needs an architecture decision record, and the per-commit Developer Certificate of Origin.
osps_le_01_01_justification: A Developer Certificate of Origin (1.1) is required of every contributor and documented in CONTRIBUTING.md. It is enforced by .github/workflows/dco.yml, which fails a pull request when any commit in it lacks a Signed-off-by trailer, and that check is a required status check on main.
osps_qa_03_01_justification: The main branch ruleset requires six status checks under the strict up-to-date policy: the deployment-floor build/test/launch gate, the DCO sign-off check, the three CodeQL analyses, and the dependency review. They must pass before a commit reaches main.
osps_qa_06_01_justification: macos26-floor.yml runs the NepalKitCore suite (swift test), the app-layer suite (scripts/run-app-tests.sh) and the Watch suite on every pull request to main, and its job is a required status check, so no change reaches main without an automated test run.
osps_sa_01_01_justification: CONTEXT.md plus fourteen architecture decision records in docs/adr/ describe the system's actors and their actions: the menu-bar app, the SwiftUI surfaces, NepalKitCore's calendar engine, the Sparkle updater and its feed, the Watch app and complications, the calendar data pipeline, and the release pipeline. docs/achievements.md records what that structure has produced.
osps_sa_02_01_justification: The released external interfaces are documented: README.md documents the three Siri and Shortcuts intents and the fields they return, the four Watch complication styles, the menu-bar and Settings surfaces; docs/release-verification.md documents the update feed and its enclosure contract; and ADR-0008 documents the sandbox entitlements that define the app's external interaction surface.
osps_sa_03_01_justification: docs/security-assessment.md records a dated security assessment covering v1.6.0: the method and its stated limits, eight findings F1 to F8 ranked by realistic impact with the mitigation and the residual risk for each, and a list of things looked for and not found. It names the update path as the asset that matters most, and explains what 'the gate is green' does and does not mean - including that a CodeQL alert does not block a merge, which is finding F8.
osps_vm_01_01_justification: SECURITY.md is a coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy with a clear response expectation (acknowledgement within a few days), a 90-day disclosure window, and a statement that the timeline can be extended on request rather than the reporter going quiet.
osps_vm_03_01_justification: SECURITY.md gives a monitored email address as the private reporting path and directs reporters to file a GitHub Security Advisory from the repository's own Security tab, so reports do not have to be public.
osps_vm_04_01_justification: Disclosed vulnerabilities are published as GitHub Security Advisories on this repository, at a fixed public URL readable without an account. SECURITY.md names that channel, states that a confirmed issue gets an advisory there before it is described publicly anywhere, and records that each advisory names the affected versions, how a user can tell whether they are affected, and what to do; release notes link to the advisory when there is one. No advisory has been published yet because no vulnerability has been reported, and the policy says so explicitly rather than leaving an empty channel unexplained.
osps_ac_04_02_justification: Permissions are set per job, not only workflow-wide. pages.yml grants pages: write and id-token: write solely to deploy; release-tag.yml grants contents: read only to the two jobs that check out code, and nothing at all to the rest.
osps_br_01_04_justification: No workflow accepts collaborator input. Every workflow_dispatch-enabled workflow (data-sources, macos26-floor, codeql, pages) declares no inputs at all, so there is no manual value to sanitise.
osps_br_02_02_justification: Every asset is named from the release identifier: the Sparkle enclosure, the cask version and the DMG and zip all derive from MARKETING_VERSION, and the preflight refuses a tag that does not match it.
osps_br_07_02_justification: docs/secrets-policy.md inventories every credential, where each is stored, who can reach it, the rule that no pull_request workflow references a secret, rotation per credential, and the ordered leak response.
osps_do_03_01_justification: docs/release-verification.md gives commands and expected output: shasum -a 256, codesign -dv, xcrun stapler validate (must pass offline), and spctl -a -t execute expecting source=Notarized Developer ID. All are automated in the release scripts.
osps_do_03_02_justification: The same document states the expected identity, Developer ID Application: Dibas Sigdel (CA89X9954L), how to read it with codesign -dv, and that the document is not itself a trust anchor: Apple's notarization record is.
osps_do_04_01_justification: SUPPORT.md and SECURITY.md state scope and duration: fixes land on the latest release, there is no long-term-support branch, and backporting would cost more than it saves.
osps_do_05_01_justification: SECURITY.md's supported-versions table states that anything older than the latest release no longer receives security updates.
osps_gv_04_01_justification: GOVERNANCE.md requires confirming a defensible lineage of identity before granting write access, merge rights, release authority or secret access, per person and per resource, with a higher bar for secrets. CODEOWNERS enforces review on the updater, entitlements, Info.plist and licence.
osps_qa_02_02_justification: No software bill of materials is generated or delivered with released assets. GitHub produces an SPDX document for the dependency graph, but nothing is attached to a release and package-release.sh emits none.
osps_qa_04_02_justification: Single repository; no subprojects are compiled into a release.
osps_qa_06_02_justification: README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md give each test suite's exact command, the order check-all.sh runs its eleven gates, and the rule that a skipped test reports a reason rather than passing.
osps_qa_06_03_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md requires a behaviour change to ship with a matching test change in the same commit, and enumerates what counts as major: any calendar change, user-visible or spoken value, App Intent, release-contract artifact, or bug fix.
osps_qa_07_01_justification: The main ruleset requires maintainer approval, so merging is a deliberate act separate from pushing. Stated plainly: the owner is also a bypass actor, so this is not separation of duties against them, and GitHub does not permit self-approval, so a second approver is needed to satisfy this with a non-author. Tracked as finding F3.
osps_sa_03_02_justification: docs/threat-model.md ranks seven assets, names six actor classes, draws six trust boundaries, and analyses ten threats with the control in front of each and the residual risk left. It records what is out of scope and what would invalidate each claim.
osps_vm_04_02_justification: No VEX document is published. There is no known dependency vulnerability assessed as non-exploitable to augment a report with; docs/dependencies.md requires the update path be treated as Critical and a no-fix finding resolved by removal.
osps_vm_05_01_justification: docs/dependencies.md sets thresholds: Critical is release-blocking, High blocks a tagged release within 7 days, Medium 30 days, Low the next release touching the dependency. The update path is always Critical, and a finding with no upstream fix is resolved by removal rather than acceptance.
osps_vm_05_02_justification: The same section requires findings be addressed before a release: dependency review on every pull request as a required check, the Sparkle freshness job green on main before a tag, and a preflight refusing any tag whose commit is not a GitHub-verified commit on main.
osps_vm_05_03_justification: dependency-review.yml runs actions/dependency-review-action on every pull request and fails at moderate severity; the job is a required status check. Scope: this covers only graph-visible dependencies, which here are the github-actions ecosystem. Sparkle is not in the graph, so its advisories need manual review before each release.
osps_vm_06_01_justification: docs/security-assessment.md sets SAST thresholds: any finding in the update path, entitlements or Info.plist before the next release; error 7 days; warning 30 days; note the next release touching the file. Suppression to get a green build is forbidden, and there is no CodeQL allowlist.
osps_vm_06_02_justification: CodeQL analyses run on every pull request for Swift, Python and Actions. Four separate evaluators report alongside it - SonarCloud's quality gate, CodeRabbit, GitGuardian, and GitHub's own AI code-scanning findings - and not one of them blocks a merge: the ruleset has no code-scanning-results rule, does not require the Sonar, CodeRabbit, GitGuardian or AI-scanning checks, and a failing required check can be waived by the actor who is already the bypass actor. Evaluation is enforced; blocking is not. One-rule fix recorded as finding F8.
access_continuity_justification: One maintainer. GOVERNANCE.md states there is no succession plan.
accessibility_best_practices_justificati: Every surface is labelled, VoiceOver is tested, and CODING_STANDARDS.md makes it non-optional.
assurance_case_justification: docs/assurance-case.md is a structured claim about NepalKit 1.6.0 with the scope limited in the first paragraph, four sub-claims each depending on the one beneath it, evidence cited per step, residual risk named, the evidence that is missing listed, and five falsification conditions of which three are already gates.
automated_integration_testing_justificat: The suites are unit and app-layer; nothing exercises the built app's components together.
build_justification: xcodebuild plus scripts/check-all.sh, which builds, lints, and tests.
build_floss_tools_justification: Xcode, SwiftPM, Homebrew, Python 3, all FLOSS.
build_non_recursive_justification: The top-level project builds without recursing into submodules.
build_preserve_debug_justification: Debug uses DEBUG_INFORMATION_FORMAT = dwarf, so a local build is fully debuggable; only Release packages a dSYM.
build_repeatable_justification: A clean checkout builds the same way; the floor gate asserts it on every PR.
build_reproducible_justification: No byte-for-byte reproducibility claim is made or tested.
build_standard_variables_justification: Standard Xcode build settings and environment conventions.
bus_factor_justification: One person holds all knowledge. Recorded as finding F3.
code_of_conduct_justification: CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md at the repository root, referenced from CONTRIBUTING.md.
code_review_standards_justification: CODEOWNERS makes review mandatory on sensitive paths; CONTRIBUTING sets the standard.
coding_standards_justification: CODING_STANDARDS.md, described in CONTRIBUTING as non-advisory.
coding_standards_enforced_justification: SwiftLint --strict runs in CI and the ruleset requires it.
contribution_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md, linked from README, documents the whole contribution process.
contributors_unassociated_justification: No policy on unaffiliated contributions. One commit of 338 carries a different author identity, TheBoss, which is not a collaborator and has never had push access; whether that is the same individual under a second account or a genuine outside contribution is not something the repository can establish. docs/achievements.md records it rather than resolving it.
copyright_per_file_justification: Every Swift file carries an SPDX identifier and copyright line.
crypto_algorithm_agility_justification: The update signature algorithm is fixed by Sparkle and cannot be swapped here.
crypto_call_justification: The app calls Sparkle's cryptography and implements none of its own.
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: Notarization is stapled and validated; Sparkle verifies the feed and archive signatures.
crypto_credential_agility_justification: Key rotation is documented but manual; no re-signing path is automated.
crypto_keylength_justification: Ed25519 with its standard key size.
crypto_password_storage_justification: The app stores no passwords and has no accounts.
crypto_pfs_justification: No session keys are negotiated; the update channel uses static signatures.
crypto_random_justification: The app generates no random values of its own.
crypto_tls12_justification: No explicit TLS minimum is configured. The app relies on the OS default, which is not a floor the project sets.
crypto_used_network_justification: One network call in the whole product: the HTTPS update check.
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: Ed25519 verification against a public key in the signed binary.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: No known weakness in Ed25519 or in Sparkle's use of it.
crypto_working_justification: The signature path is exercised by the appcast gate on every change to the feed.
dco_justification: dco.yml fails a pull request with an unsigned commit, and it is a required status check.
delivery_mitm_justification: HTTPS, Apple notarization, and an Ed25519-signed feed and archive.
delivery_unsigned_justification: The app refuses an unsigned feed, and a release is notarized and stapled.
dependency_monitoring_justification: Dependabot watches the Actions ecosystem; a scheduled job checks the Sparkle pin.
description_good_justification: README opens with a one-sentence statement of what the app is.
discussion_justification: GitHub Issues are enabled and SUPPORT.md names them as the channel.
documentation_achievements_justification: docs/achievements.md records what shipped in one place, with the shell commands to recount every number so a reader can check rather than trust. It also records who has contributed, including the one commit authored by a non-collaborator account, and what has NOT been achieved.
documentation_architecture_justification: CONTEXT.md plus fourteen architecture decision records in docs/adr/ describe the system's actors and their actions: the menu-bar app, the SwiftUI surfaces, NepalKitCore's calendar engine, the Sparkle updater and its feed, the Watch app and complications, the calendar data pipeline, and the release pipeline.
documentation_basics_justification: README covers what it is, requirements, install, usage, and licence.
documentation_current_justification: README documents current behaviour; the data-sources gate fails when the calendar or its documented provenance diverges.
documentation_interface_justification: README documents the menu bar, popover, Settings, converter, Siri/Shortcuts and the Watch app.
documentation_quick_start_justification: README Install section is a download-and-drag or brew one-liner.
documentation_roadmap_justification: docs/roadmap.md names what is planned, what is deliberately not planned and why, and for each planned item the blocking condition rather than a date. It states that the badge answer is Met on the strength of the file naming its blockers, so the coupling is explicit.
documentation_security_justification: SECURITY.md: contacts, scope, CVD policy, threat model.
dynamic_analysis_justification: No dynamic analysis or fuzzing exists.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: No dynamic analysis runs, so there is no analysis build with assertions enabled.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No dynamic analysis has produced findings to fix.
english_justification: Documentation and code comments are in English.
enhancement_responses_justification: No enhancement request has been answered, so there is no record.
external_dependencies_justification: docs/dependencies.md is the complete inventory with selection and tracking.
floss_license_justification: GPL-3.0-or-later in LICENSE at the repository root.
governance_justification: GOVERNANCE.md names the decision-maker and what that means.
hardened_site_justification: There is no website to harden; only a static appcast on GitHub Pages.
hardening_justification: package-release.sh fails the release unless the hardened runtime flag is present.
implement_secure_design_justification: docs/threat-model.md and ADR-0008 record the design and its least-privilege entitlements.
input_validation_justification: Conversion returns explicit unsupported and error states rather than a plausible wrong answer.
installation_common_justification: A signed notarized DMG plus a Homebrew cask.
installation_development_quick_justifica: README: clone, open the project, run the scheme.
installation_standard_variables_justific: Standard install locations and paths throughout the release scripts.
interact_justification: README documents install and upgrade; SUPPORT.md names where to report bugs.
interfaces_current_justification: README and the release-verification doc describe the interfaces as they ship.
internationalization_justification: Latin and Devanagari digits, Nepali and transliterated names, and a string catalog.
know_common_errors_justification: There is no training record for the developers.
know_secure_design_justification: There is no training record for the developers.
maintained_justification: Eight releases and active commits in the week the entry was created.
maintenance_or_update_justification: SUPPORT.md and SECURITY.md state that fixes land on the latest release.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: Secret scanning and push protection are enabled, and no credential is in the repository.
regression_tests_added50_justification: No regression-suite percentage is measured. The 93-test core suite is largely property-based round-tripping rather than per-defect regressions, and nothing classifies tests that way.
release_notes_justification: CHANGELOG.md per version, plus release pages and appcast entries.
release_notes_vulns_justification: No release has documented a vulnerability fix, because none has been found.
repo_distributed_justification: GitHub releases carry a signed notarized DMG; Homebrew distributes it as a cask.
repo_interim_justification: MARKETING_VERSION and CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION distinguish interim builds from releases.
repo_public_justification: Public repository at a stable URL.
repo_track_justification: Git, with public history and no force-push on the default branch.
report_archive_justification: GitHub Issues are permanent and searchable; delete_branch_on_merge is off.
report_process_justification: SUPPORT.md documents where, what to include, and how triage works.
report_responses_justification: No bug report has been closed, so responsiveness is not demonstrated.
require_2FA_justification: GitHub offers no MFA enforcement for a repository owned by a user account.
roles_responsibilities_justification: GOVERNANCE.md 'Who decides' and 'What that means in practice'.
secure_2FA_justification: Same: there is no mechanism to require or attest second-factor use.
security_review_justification: No independent security review has been performed.
signed_releases_justification: Releases are Developer ID signed, notarized, stapled, and Ed25519-signed in the appcast.
sites_https_justification: The only site is GitHub Pages over HTTPS; every other channel is HTTPS or SSH.
sites_password_security_justification: No accounts, no login, no stored passwords anywhere.
small_tasks_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md's 'Size of a change' sets a ~400-line guideline, says when to split and when to keep together, and names two deliberate exceptions. It states plainly that this is a policy rather than a measurement: nothing in the history has been tracked as a multi-week issue, so the claim is that changes are small, not that they are decomposed.
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL over Swift, Python and Actions, plus SwiftLint and SonarCloud.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL's default query suite covers the common vulnerability patterns.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: Twelve code-scanning alerts were closed, four of them by changing the code rather than the config.
static_analysis_often_justification: CodeQL runs on every push and pull request and weekly on a schedule.
test_justification: Three automated suites run on every pull request.
test_branch_coverage80_justification: Swift emits no branch data, so llvm-cov's Branches column is zero and is not quoted. The nearest equivalent, llvm-cov region coverage, is 57.48% combined. docs/coverage.md names it regions rather than branches for that reason.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: Six required status checks run on every pull request to main.
test_invocation_justification: README and CONTRIBUTING give the exact command for each suite.
test_most_justification: 43.96% combined statement coverage does not support a claim that most functionality is tested. The calendar engine at 85.62% plausibly does; the app layer at 35.03% does not. Both figures are measured by scripts/measure-coverage.py and recorded in docs/coverage.md.
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING requires a behaviour change to ship with a test change.
test_policy_mandated_justification: The same policy, and CI refuses a merge whose gates did not run.
test_statement_coverage80_justification: Measured 43.96% combined statement coverage by scripts/measure-coverage.py: 85.62% over NepalKitCore's nine source files and 35.03% over the app layer's 42. docs/coverage.md explains why the gap is a view-logic refactor rather than a test-writing chore, and 1,352 lines across six SwiftUI views sit at 0%.
test_statement_coverage90_justification: 43.96% combined statement coverage, measured and published by scripts/measure-coverage.py. The gate has a floor and deliberately no target; docs/coverage.md argues why a target above the truth would fail every day.
tests_are_added_justification: Tests accompany behaviour changes, and the suites have grown with the product.
tests_documented_added_justification: CONTRIBUTING enumerates exactly which changes require tests.
two_person_review_justification: A single maintainer cannot obtain a second reviewer.
updateable_reused_components_justificati: Sparkle is pinned to an exact version and a scheduled job fails when upstream moves.
version_semver_justification: SemVer tags, and the release preflight refuses a tag that disagrees with MARKETING_VERSION.
version_tags_justification: Every release is a v* tag on main.
version_tags_signed_justification: Release tags are signed with the same SSH key the commits use. release-tag.yml documents `git tag -s` plus `gh release create --verify-tag`, and the flag is load-bearing: without it gh creates a lightweight tag, which carries no signature. docs/release-verification.md step 2 verifies a tag with `git tag -v`. Tags before v1.6.1 are lightweight and unsigned - `git cat-file -t v1.6.0` answers commit, not tag - which the document states rather than glossing.
version_unique_justification: The preflight refuses any tag that does not match the app's MARKETING_VERSION.
